notIdeasOfWhatSocietyShouldBe.explanation: The defining sources (Britannica, EBSCO, the Kent glossary, Blankholm, the Zurich nonreligion page) define irreligion as the lack or rejection of religious belief or practice and as an umbrella over atheism, agnosticism, skepticism, rationalism and secularism; Britannica says it 'does not require the active support of any of these positions'. I went through every religion, state, public-life, education, law and speech statement (separate-church-state, more-religion-public, reason-over-faith, no-religion-state-schools, punish-blasphemy, apostasy-punishable, restrict-conversion, state-promotes-atheism, religion-illusion and the rest) and found none that the sources state as irreligion's own position: the political content they mention (minimising religion in public life) belongs to the secularism strand, whose sources are not irreligion's, and the rest is definition, history and demography.
